The area of the region bounded by y=x2y = x^2y=x2, the x-axis and the lines x=0x = 0x=0 and x=3x = 3x=3 is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area under y=f(x)≥0y=f(x)\ge 0y=f(x)≥0 from x=ax=ax=a to x=bx=bx=b is ∫aby dx\int_a^b y\,dx∫ab​ydx.

  1. 1

    Write the area as an integral.

    A=∫03x2 dxA = \displaystyle\int_0^3 x^2\,dxA=∫03​x2dx
  2. 2

    Integrate and put the limits.

    A=[x33]03=273−0=9A = \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^3 = \dfrac{27}{3} - 0 = 9A=[3x3​]03​=327​−0=9A=[x33]03=273−0=9\displaystyle A = \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^3 = \dfrac{27}{3} - 0 = 9A=[3x3​]03​=327​−0=9
    1
  3. 3

    So the area is 999 sq units, option (B).

Answer(B) 9\displaystyle 99 sq units

Watch out Forgetting to divide by 333 and choosing 272727.

2MCQ1 mark
The area enclosed by the circle x2+y2=4x^2 + y^2 = 4x2+y2=4 is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area of the circle x2+y2=r2x^2+y^2=r^2x2+y2=r2 is πr2\pi r^2πr2.

  1. 1

    Compare with x2+y2=r2x^2 + y^2 = r^2x2+y2=r2.

    r2=4⇒r=2r^2 = 4 \Rightarrow r = 2r2=4⇒r=2
  2. 2

    Use area =πr2= \pi r^2=πr2.

    A=π(2)2=4πA = \pi (2)^2 = 4\piA=π(2)2=4π

    Same as 4∫024−x2 dx4\int_0^2\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx4∫02​4−x2​dx.

    1
  3. 3

    So the area is 4π4\pi4π sq units, option (B).

Answer(B) 4π\displaystyle 4\pi4π sq units

Watch out Using r=4r = 4r=4 instead of r=2r = 2r=2 and choosing 16π16\pi16π.

The area of the region bounded by y=cos⁡xy = \cos xy=cosx, the x-axis, x=0x = 0x=0 and x=π2x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}x=2π​ is:

Tap the option you think is right.

  1. 1

    Write the area as an integral.

    A=∫0π/2cos⁡x dxA = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos x\,dxA=∫0π/2​cosxdxA=∫0π/2cos⁡x dx\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos x\,dxA=∫0π/2​cosxdx

    cos⁡x≥0\cos x \ge 0cosx≥0 on [0,π2]\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right][0,2π​].

  2. 2

    Integrate and put the limits.

    A=[sin⁡x]0π/2=sin⁡π2−sin⁡0=1−0=1A = \left[\sin x\right]_0^{\pi/2} = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin 0 = 1 - 0 = 1A=[sinx]0π/2​=sin2π​−sin0=1−0=1A=[sin⁡x]0π/2=sin⁡π2−sin⁡0=1−0=1\displaystyle A = \left[\sin x\right]_0^{\pi/2} = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin 0 = 1 - 0 = 1A=[sinx]0π/2​=sin2π​−sin0=1−0=1
    1
  3. 3

    So the area is 111 sq unit, option (B).

Answer(B) 1\displaystyle 11 sq unit

Question 4Question 6

Question 6 of 20, Level 1

6Assertion-Reason1 mark
Assertion (A): The area bounded by y=sin⁡xy = \sin xy=sinx and the x-axis between x=0x = 0x=0 and x=2πx = 2\pix=2π is 444 sq units. Reason (R): ∫02πsin⁡x dx=0\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi} \sin x\,dx = 0∫02π​sinxdx=0.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area uses ∣sin⁡x∣|\sin x|∣sinx∣: split where the curve crosses the x-axis.

  1. 1

    Assertion: sin⁡x<0\sin x < 0sinx<0 on (π,2π)(\pi, 2\pi)(π,2π), so split at π\piπ.

    A=∫0πsin⁡x dx+∣∫π2πsin⁡x dx∣=2+∣−2∣=4\begin{aligned} A &= \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\sin x\,dx + \left|\int_{\pi}^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx\right| \\ &= 2 + |-2| = 4 \end{aligned}A​=∫0π​sinxdx+​∫π2π​sinxdx​=2+∣−2∣=4​
  2. 2

    So A is true.

  3. 3

    Reason: integrate straight from 000 to 2π2\pi2π.

    ∫02πsin⁡x dx=[−cos⁡x]02π=−1+1=0\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx = \left[-\cos x\right]_0^{2\pi} = -1 + 1 = 0∫02π​sinxdx=[−cosx]02π​=−1+1=0∫02πsin⁡x dx=[−cos⁡x]02π=−1+1=0\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx = \left[-\cos x\right]_0^{2\pi} = -1 + 1 = 0∫02π​sinxdx=[−cosx]02π​=−1+1=0
  4. 4

    So R is true.

  5. 5

    R gives 000 because the parts cancel; it does not give the area 444.

    1
  6. 6

    So R is not the correct explanation of A: option (B).

Answer(B) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

Watch out Thinking area =∫02πsin⁡x dx=0= \int_0^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx = 0=∫02π​sinxdx=0 and marking A false.

Question 5Question 7

Question 7 of 20, Level 1

7Short answer2 marks
Find the area of the region bounded by y2=xy^2 = xy2=x, the x-axis and the lines x=1x = 1x=1 and x=4x = 4x=4, lying in the first quadrant.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area =∫aby dx= \int_a^b y\,dx=∫ab​ydx, with yyy taken from the curve.

  1. 1

    Draw a rough sketch and shade the region from x=1x = 1x=1 to x=4x = 4x=4.

  2. 2

    In the first quadrant, take the positive root.

    y2=x⇒y=xy^2 = x \Rightarrow y = \sqrt{x}y2=x⇒y=x​
  3. 3

    Write the required area.

    A=∫14y dx=∫14x dxA = \displaystyle\int_1^4 y\,dx = \int_1^4 \sqrt{x}\,dxA=∫14​ydx=∫14​x​dxA=∫14y dx=∫14x dx\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_1^4 y\,dx = \int_1^4 \sqrt{x}\,dxA=∫14​ydx=∫14​x​dx
    1
  4. 4

    Integrate.

    A=[23x3/2]14A = \left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_1^4A=[32​x3/2]14​A=[23x3/2]14\displaystyle A = \left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_1^4A=[32​x3/2]14​
    ½
  5. 5

    Put the limits.

    A=23(43/2−13/2)=23(8−1)=143A = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(4^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}(8 - 1) = \dfrac{14}{3}A=32​(43/2−13/2)=32​(8−1)=314​A=23(43/2−13/2)=23(8−1)=143\displaystyle A = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(4^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}(8 - 1) = \dfrac{14}{3}A=32​(43/2−13/2)=32​(8−1)=314​

    43/2=(4)3=84^{3/2} = (\sqrt{4})^3 = 843/2=(4​)3=8

  6. 6

    Hence the required area =143= \dfrac{14}{3}=314​ sq units.

    ½
Answer143\displaystyle \dfrac{14}{3}314​ sq units

Watch out Taking 43/24^{3/2}43/2 as 666 instead of 888.

Find the area of the region bounded by y2=9xy^2 = 9xy2=9x, x=2x = 2x=2, x=4x = 4x=4 and the x-axis in the first quadrant.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area =∫aby dx= \int_a^b y\,dx=∫ab​ydx, with yyy taken from the curve.

  1. 1

    Draw a rough sketch and shade the region from x=2x = 2x=2 to x=4x = 4x=4.

    ½
  2. 2

    In the first quadrant, take the positive root.

    y2=9x⇒y=3xy^2 = 9x \Rightarrow y = 3\sqrt{x}y2=9x⇒y=3x​
  3. 3

    Write the required area.

    A=∫24y dx=∫243x dxA = \displaystyle\int_2^4 y\,dx = \int_2^4 3\sqrt{x}\,dxA=∫24​ydx=∫24​3x​dxA=∫24y dx=∫243x dx\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_2^4 y\,dx = \int_2^4 3\sqrt{x}\,dxA=∫24​ydx=∫24​3x​dx
    1
  4. 4

    Integrate.

    A=3[23x3/2]24=2[x3/2]24A = 3\left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_2^4 = 2\left[x^{3/2}\right]_2^4A=3[32​x3/2]24​=2[x3/2]24​A=3[23x3/2]24=2[x3/2]24\displaystyle A = 3\left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_2^4 = 2\left[x^{3/2}\right]_2^4A=3[32​x3/2]24​=2[x3/2]24​
    ½
  5. 5

    Put the limits.

    A=2(43/2−23/2)=2(8−22)A = 2\left(4^{3/2} - 2^{3/2}\right) = 2\left(8 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)A=2(43/2−23/2)=2(8−22​)A=2(43/2−23/2)=2(8−22)\displaystyle A = 2\left(4^{3/2} - 2^{3/2}\right) = 2\left(8 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)A=2(43/2−23/2)=2(8−22​)

    23/2=222^{3/2} = 2\sqrt{2}23/2=22​

    ½
  6. 6

    Hence the required area =16−42= 16 - 4\sqrt{2}=16−42​ sq units.

    ½
Answer16−42\displaystyle 16 - 4\sqrt{2}16−42​ sq units

Watch out Writing 23/22^{3/2}23/2 as 333 or as 2\sqrt{2}2​; it is 222\sqrt{2}22​.

Find the area of the region bounded by x2=4yx^2 = 4yx2=4y, y=2y = 2y=2, y=4y = 4y=4 and the y-axis in the first quadrant.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area between a curve and the y-axis from y=cy=cy=c to y=dy=dy=d is ∫cdx dy\int_c^d x\,dy∫cd​xdy.

  1. 1

    Draw a rough sketch and shade the region between the y-axis and the curve.

    ½
  2. 2

    The region is bounded by the y-axis, so integrate w.r.t. yyy.

  3. 3

    In the first quadrant, express xxx in terms of yyy.

    x2=4y⇒x=2yx^2 = 4y \Rightarrow x = 2\sqrt{y}x2=4y⇒x=2y​
  4. 4

    Write the required area.

    A=∫24x dy=∫242y dyA = \displaystyle\int_2^4 x\,dy = \int_2^4 2\sqrt{y}\,dyA=∫24​xdy=∫24​2y​dyA=∫24x dy=∫242y dy\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_2^4 x\,dy = \int_2^4 2\sqrt{y}\,dyA=∫24​xdy=∫24​2y​dy
    1
  5. 5

    Integrate.

    A=2[23y3/2]24=43[y3/2]24A = 2\left[\dfrac{2}{3}y^{3/2}\right]_2^4 = \dfrac{4}{3}\left[y^{3/2}\right]_2^4A=2[32​y3/2]24​=34​[y3/2]24​A=2[23y3/2]24=43[y3/2]24\displaystyle A = 2\left[\dfrac{2}{3}y^{3/2}\right]_2^4 = \dfrac{4}{3}\left[y^{3/2}\right]_2^4A=2[32​y3/2]24​=34​[y3/2]24​
    ½
  6. 6

    Put the limits.

    A=43(8−22)A = \dfrac{4}{3}\left(8 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)A=34​(8−22​)A=43(8−22)\displaystyle A = \dfrac{4}{3}\left(8 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)A=34​(8−22​)
    ½
  7. 7

    Hence the required area =32−823= \dfrac{32 - 8\sqrt{2}}{3}=332−82​​ sq units.

    ½
Answer32−823\displaystyle \dfrac{32 - 8\sqrt{2}}{3}332−82​​ sq units

Watch out Integrating w.r.t. xxx; here the strips are horizontal, so use dydydy.

Question 8Question 10

Question 10 of 20, Level 2

10Short answer3 marks
Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the line y=3x+2y = 3x + 2y=3x+2, the x-axis and the ordinates x=−1x = -1x=−1 and x=1x = 1x=1.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea A part of the region below the x-axis is taken with modulus.

  1. 1

    Find where the line meets the x-axis.

    3x+2=0⇒x=−233x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{2}{3}3x+2=0⇒x=−32​3x+2=0⇒x=−23\displaystyle 3x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{2}{3}3x+2=0⇒x=−32​

    Line is below the x-axis for x<−23x < -\frac{2}{3}x<−32​.

  2. 2

    Draw a rough sketch; the region has two parts A1A_1A1​ and A2A_2A2​.

    ½
  3. 3

    Split at x=−23x = -\dfrac{2}{3}x=−32​ and write the area.

    A=∣∫−1−2/3(3x+2) dx∣+∫−2/31(3x+2) dxA = \left|\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{-2/3}(3x+2)\,dx\right| + \int_{-2/3}^{1}(3x+2)\,dxA=​∫−1−2/3​(3x+2)dx​+∫−2/31​(3x+2)dxA=∣∫−1−2/3(3x+2) dx∣+∫−2/31(3x+2) dx\displaystyle A = \left|\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{-2/3}(3x+2)\,dx\right| + \int_{-2/3}^{1}(3x+2)\,dxA=​∫−1−2/3​(3x+2)dx​+∫−2/31​(3x+2)dx
    1
  4. 4

    Evaluate the first integral.

    [3x22+2x]−1−2/3=(23−43)−(32−2)=−23+12=−16\begin{aligned} \left[\dfrac{3x^2}{2} + 2x\right]_{-1}^{-2/3} &= \left(\dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}\right) - \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 2\right) \\ &= -\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{6} \end{aligned}[23x2​+2x]−1−2/3​​=(32​−34​)−(23​−2)=−32​+21​=−61​​
    ½
  5. 5

    Evaluate the second integral.

    [3x22+2x]−2/31=72−(−23)=256\left[\dfrac{3x^2}{2} + 2x\right]_{-2/3}^{1} = \dfrac{7}{2} - \left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{25}{6}[23x2​+2x]−2/31​=27​−(−32​)=625​[3x22+2x]−2/31=72−(−23)=256\displaystyle \left[\dfrac{3x^2}{2} + 2x\right]_{-2/3}^{1} = \dfrac{7}{2} - \left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{25}{6}[23x2​+2x]−2/31​=27​−(−32​)=625​
    ½
  6. 6

    Add the two areas.

    A=∣−16∣+256=266=133A = \left|-\dfrac{1}{6}\right| + \dfrac{25}{6} = \dfrac{26}{6} = \dfrac{13}{3}A=​−61​​+625​=626​=313​A=∣−16∣+256=266=133\displaystyle A = \left|-\dfrac{1}{6}\right| + \dfrac{25}{6} = \dfrac{26}{6} = \dfrac{13}{3}A=​−61​​+625​=626​=313​
  7. 7

    Hence the required area =133= \dfrac{13}{3}=313​ sq units.

    ½
Answer133\displaystyle \dfrac{13}{3}313​ sq units

Watch out Integrating straight from −1-1−1 to 111 gives 444, which is wrong.

    Solve for yyy in the first quadrant.

  3. 3

    Write the required area.

    1
  4. 4

    Integrate using the a2−x2\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}a2−x2​ formula with a=4a = 4a=4.

    A=34[x216−x2+8sin⁡−1x4]04A = \dfrac{3}{4}\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16 - x^2} + 8\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}\right]_0^4A=43​[2x​16−x2​+8sin−14x​]04​A=34[x216−x2+8sin⁡−1x4]04\displaystyle A = \dfrac{3}{4}\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16 - x^2} + 8\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}\right]_0^4A=43​[2x​16−x2​+8sin−14x​]04​
    ½
  5. 5

    Put the limits.

    A=34[(0+8⋅π2)−0]=34×4πA = \dfrac{3}{4}\left[\left(0 + 8\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 0\right] = \dfrac{3}{4}\times 4\piA=43​[(0+8⋅2π​)−0]=43​×4πA=34[(0+8⋅π2)−0]=34×4π\displaystyle A = \dfrac{3}{4}\left[\left(0 + 8\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 0\right] = \dfrac{3}{4}\times 4\piA=43​[(0+8⋅2π​)−0]=43​×4π

    sin⁡−11=π2\sin^{-1}1 = \frac{\pi}{2}sin−11=2π​, sin⁡−10=0\sin^{-1}0 = 0sin−10=0

  6. 6

    Hence the required area =3π= 3\pi=3π sq units.

Answer3π\displaystyle 3\pi3π sq units

Find the area of the region bounded by the parabola y2=4axy^2 = 4axy2=4ax and its latus rectum.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Latus rectum of y2=4axy^2 = 4axy2=4ax is the line x=ax = ax=a through the focus S(a,0)S(a, 0)S(a,0).

  1. 1

    Put x=ax = ax=a in the parabola to find the ends of the latus rectum.

    y2=4a2⇒y=±2ay^2 = 4a^2 \Rightarrow y = \pm 2ay2=4a2⇒y=±2a
    ½
  2. 2

    So L(a,2a)L(a, 2a)L(a,2a) and L′(a,−2a)L'(a, -2a)L′(a,−2a); draw the sketch.

    ½
  3. 3

    The region is symmetric about the x-axis.

    A=2∫0ay dx=2∫0a2ax dxA = 2\displaystyle\int_0^a y\,dx = 2\int_0^a 2\sqrt{ax}\,dxA=2∫0a​ydx=2∫0a​2ax​dxA=2∫0ay dx=2∫0a2ax dx\displaystyle A = 2\displaystyle\int_0^a y\,dx = 2\int_0^a 2\sqrt{ax}\,dxA=2∫0a​ydx=2∫0a​2ax​dx

    Area OLL′=2×OLL' = 2\timesOLL′=2× area OLSOLSOLS.

    1
  4. 4

    Integrate.

    A=4a[23x3/2]0a=8a3⋅a3/2A = 4\sqrt{a}\left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_0^a = \dfrac{8\sqrt{a}}{3}\cdot a^{3/2}A=4a​[32​x3/2]0a​=38a​​⋅a3/2A=4a[23x3/2]0a=8a3⋅a3/2\displaystyle A = 4\sqrt{a}\left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_0^a = \dfrac{8\sqrt{a}}{3}\cdot a^{3/2}A=4a​[32​x3/2]0a​=38a​​⋅a3/2
    ½
  5. 5

    Simplify: a⋅a3/2=a2\sqrt{a}\cdot a^{3/2} = a^2a​⋅a3/2=a2.

    A=8a23A = \dfrac{8a^2}{3}A=38a2​

Answer8a23\displaystyle \dfrac{8a^2}{3}38a2​ sq units

Case Study: A running track in a sports complex is in the shape of the ellipse x236+y216=1\dfrac{x^2}{36} + \dfrac{y^2}{16} = 136x2​+16y2​=1 (units in metres). The region inside the track is to be grassed.
  1. (i)Find the total area enclosed by the track.1 mark
  2. (ii)Find the area of the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the track and the axes.1 mark
  3. (iii)Find the area of the region inside the track between x=0x = 0x=0 and x=3x = 3x=3 in the first quadrant.2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area of an ellipse is πab\pi abπab; part areas use ∫a2−x2 dx\int\sqrt{a^2-x^2}\,dx∫a2−x2​dx.

(i)1 mark

  1. 1

    Compare with x2a2+y2b2=1\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1a2x2​+b2y2​=1.

    a=6,b=4a = 6,\quad b = 4a=6,b=4
  2. 2

    Use area of ellipse =πab= \pi ab=πab.

    A=π(6)(4)=24πA = \pi(6)(4) = 24\piA=π(6)(4)=24π
    1
  3. 3

    Total area enclosed =24π m2= 24\pi\ \text{m}^2=24π m2.

Answer (i)24π m2\displaystyle 24\pi\ \text{m}^224π m2

(ii)1 mark

    A=14×24π=6πA = \dfrac{1}{4}\times 24\pi = 6\piA=41​×24π=6π

  2. 2

    First-quadrant area =6π m2= 6\pi\ \text{m}^2=6π m2.

Answer (ii)6π m2\displaystyle 6\pi\ \text{m}^26π m2
